newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE oil revenue $9.05 bln in 1995 - Central Bank.
newsitem.headline: UAE oil revenue $9.05 bln in 1995 - Central Bank.

text.p: United Arab Emirates (UAE) consolidated government oil revenue hit 33.23 billion dirhams ($9.05 billion) in 1995, preliminary Central Bank figures show.

Oil was the biggest contributor to total federal government revenue of 43.65 billion dirhams ($11.89 billion), preliminary figures in the Bank's statistical bulletin for the second quarter of this year show.
On the current account, oil exports were valued at 44.59 billion dirhams and natural gas exports were 5.5 billion of total exports and re-exports of 103.06 billion.
The UAE is a federation of seven members -- each of which have separate budgets. Not all incomes accruing to each emirate are channelled into the federal treasury.
Abu Dhabi accounts for over 90 percent of UAE oil output.
The Bank said the average price of oil last year was $16.64 a barrel, up from $15.57 the previous year.
Petroleum prices this year have revisted their highest level since the 1990-1991 Gulf War, opening the way for further gains in UAE oil income.
OPEC member UAE has a production quota of 2.16 million barrels per day (bpd).
